A new, friendlier interface, a GD&T frame builder that reads your frame back in plain words, dimensions and tolerances written inside any text -- and a much faster start.

### A new interface
- **Top bar** instead of the menu bar and toolbar: menu button, document name with an "unsaved" marker, a search field, Undo / Redo, light / dark switch and a Save button.
- **Search any command with Ctrl+K**: every menu command, every tool and your recent files. Results are grouped by menu, your typing is highlighted, shortcuts are shown as keys, and the commands you use most come first. Before you type, it lists what you used last and your recent files.
- **Tool rail** on the left, one icon per tool. Line / Arrow / Double arrow and the stamp text are chosen from a small flyout before you draw.
- **On the canvas**: a hint that tells you what the current tool does, and a page / zoom pill (previous / next page, type a page number, zoom presets, fit, 1:1, rotate).
- **One left panel** with two tabs: **Pages** (thumbnails with the number of annotations on each page, drag to reorder) and **Annotations** (grouped by page, named after their content, filter by type or text; click one to select it, even on another page).
- **Inspector** on the right: everything about the selection in one place -- style, shape, text, line ends, stamp, GD&T frame, position and size in mm or pt, arrange. With nothing selected it sets the color and stroke of the next annotation. Stroke presets plus an exact value; **your own color palette** (rename, reorder, add, remove, reset).
- **Start page**: drop a PDF anywhere, Open PDF / New blank document, recent files as cards with a thumbnail, folder, date, page count and annotation count (right-click: Open, Show in Folder, Remove from List).
- IBM Plex fonts, consistent light and dark themes.

### GD&T frame builder
- Replaces the former frame editor, for new frames and for editing (double-click).
- The 14 ISO 1101 symbols in a grid by family, zone (width, Ø, SØ, R, SR), value, modifier (Ⓜ Ⓛ Ⓟ Ⓔ), datums with their own modifiers and common datums (A-B), notes above / below, composite frames (one characteristic per row).
- A large preview of the frame with a **plain-language read-back** ("Position within a Ø0.1 mm cylindrical zone at maximum material (MMC), relative to datums A, B, C.") and warnings for missing datums (orientation, runout, concentricity, symmetry).
- Form tolerances skip the datum step. New frames start from the last characteristic you placed.

### Text, dimensions and tolerances
- **Dimension annotation**: nominal value, prefix (Ø, R, SØ, SR, □) and a symmetric (±0.05) or bilateral (+0.10 / -0.05) tolerance.
- **Tolerances inside any text**, and a **contextual toolbar** while you type: symbols, tolerances, font size, border.
- The notes above / below a GD&T frame are real texts, with symbols and tolerances.
- Typing in a text annotation: Space, the arrow keys and editing in the middle of the text work as expected.

### Faster start
- The downloads are about five times smaller (55 MB instead of 280 MB): they no longer carry parts of Qt that Annoter does not use, so the single .exe no longer unpacks hundreds of MB at every launch.
- A splash screen shows up right away while the program starts.
- Recent-file thumbnails are kept between sessions, so the start page is ready at once.

### Fixes
- Rectangles and ellipses drawn in other software without a fill (Acrobat) no longer open filled with black.
- A boxed text annotation no longer makes saving fail.
- Placing a GD&T frame and immediately adding a note no longer deletes the frame.

### Downloads (portable, no install, Windows 64-bit)
- **Annoter-portable.zip** (recommended) -- unzip, then run `Annoter.exe` from the folder. Fastest start; keep the whole folder together. Unzip first: running it from inside the zip makes Windows unpack everything to a temporary folder.
- **Annoter.exe** -- single self-contained file: download and double-click.

**First launch on a new PC**: the files are not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may show "Windows protected your PC". Click **More info**, then **Run anyway** (once per downloaded file).
